A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stylos, with matching authors, core architecture, objectives and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and stylization experiments, baseline comparisons, attention and loss ablations, and inference-scaling measurements in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, artistic-quality and timing measurements, interpolation experiments, expanded ablation examples and failure cases.

M1.justification: V2 introduces embedding interpolation for style blending and stylization-strength control in Section 4.3. Section 3.2.2 also changes the specified hybrid variant from concatenating separate frame/global outputs to sequential frame-then-global processing. The principal global-only architecture and training objectives remain; expanded CrossBlock details alone do not establish a replaced core model.

E1.justification: V2 reports DELAUNAY as an additional style-image source and evaluates two-style blending and adjustable stylization strength. CO3D, DL3DV-10K, Tanks and Temples, and WikiArt remain the principal content/style coverage. Displaying the 50 held-out styles adds documentation rather than establishing a new test set.

E2.justification: V1 compares against StyleRF and StyleGS. V2 retains StyleGS under its full name, StyleGaussian, removes StyleRF from the reported comparisons, and adds G-Style, SGSST and Styl3R. StylizedGS participates in Figure 5 and appendix Tables 5–6, although excluded from the main quantitative tables.

E3.justification: V2 substantially broadens evaluation with ArtFID, supplementary FID, LPIPS-gray, CFSD and color-matching metrics, plus comparative stylization timing. The added timing protocol specifies common GH200 hardware, method-specific resolutions and inclusion of per-scene fitting costs. Appendix A.4 also introduces failure-case filtering for StylizedGS, although its application is not fully clear.

E4.justification: V2 expands loss ablations across additional styles in Figures 8–10, adds blending and strength-control experiments in Figure 6, and presents explicit reconstruction, unwanted-color and oversmoothing failure studies in Figures 11–13. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's attention/loss ablations and retained view-count analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly specifies comparative timing averages over 112 samples after 48 warm-up samples. This is distinct from the unchanged efficiency-scaling experiment averaged over 100 iterations in both versions. No seed-based performance uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the consistency values and adds ArtScores of 4.78, 9.12 and 9.15 for image, scene and 3D losses. For example, 3D-loss long-range LPIPS changes from 0.140 to 0.153; matching evaluation sampling is not established, so this is not a demonstrated performance regression. Tables 3–6 add substantial comparator, quality and timing results, while corresponding Stylos and StyleGaussian entries in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The hybrid-attention definition changes substantively from channel concatenation in v1 Equation 3 to sequential composition in v2 Section 3.2.2. The 3D-loss pseudocode also corrects per-view voxel statistics to joint multi-view fusion, aligning it with the existing mathematical objective. The principal style-loss equations remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution bullets and conclusion retain the central claims about feedforward, pose-free, generalizable and view-consistent stylization. The introduction makes a limited narrowing: global attention now preserves fine visual details in Gaussian renderings, replacing the earlier claim about preserving geometric details.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive applicability limits involving thin or cluttered structures, extreme palettes, lighting changes, invented colors and oversmoothing. Appendix A.5 attributes increasing-view degradation primarily to VGGT reconstruction instability, extending v1's discussion of training-view mismatch and unstable Gaussians. Appendix A.3 also develops the explanation of why independent frame conditioning harms reconstruction.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies previously missing layer counts, initialization, voxel size, optimizer, 15k-iteration training schedules, learning rates, augmentation and input sampling details. V2 also documents comparison hardware and displays the evaluation styles. Image/scene-loss pseudocode is removed and 3D-loss pseudocode revised. Code availability changes from promised to announced, although the reproducibility statement still says release will follow acceptance.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for StyTr2, G-Style, DELAUNAY, ArtFID and StyleID, and refines positioning against per-scene fitting methods and the closest feedforward competitor, Styl3R. The overall research lineage remains. Publication-year and venue updates for existing references do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the related-work discussion, attention-module explanation and experimental narratives. It reorganizes the appendix around implementation, scaling, ablations, reproducibility, limitations and visual results, replacing the earlier pseudocode-led organization. The 3D-loss algorithm moves into the main text, and acknowledgements and conference/author information are added or revised.

P2.justification: V2 revises the architecture diagram, rebuilds Figure 5 for the expanded comparisons, adds blending, ablation, failure and evaluation-style figures, and expands tables with metrics, timings and comparison highlighting. Tables 5–6 are new. The original appendix gallery is retained as Figures 16–25, and the unchanged scaling plots move from Figure 6 to Figure 7.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses substantial evidential and reproducibility gaps: v1 lacked a direct comparison with the closest feedforward competitor and supplied few training details. The expanded comparisons, implementation information and explicit failure studies substantially improve assessment of practical tradeoffs and applicability. Ambiguities remain around StylizedGS failure exclusions and code-release wording, but these do not outweigh the gains in empirical support and transparency.
